<div class="quickstart-hero">
<h1>FishSET GUI Quickstart Guide</h1>
<p>FishSET is a set of statistical programming and data management tools for organizing fishery data, creating model inputs, and evaluating policy scenarios. This guide gives new users a practical path through the FishSET GUI.</p>
<p><strong>Recommended path:</strong> Upload Data &rarr; Select variables &rarr; QAQC &rarr; Explore the data &rarr; Format Data &rarr; Modeling &rarr; Policy</p>
</div>

<div class="quickstart-grid">
<div class="quickstart-card"><h3>What the GUI does</h3><p>The GUI helps you move from raw data to model-ready outputs without writing code. It guides data loading, quality checks, derived variables, model fitting, and policy analysis.</p></div>
<div class="quickstart-card"><h3>Before you start</h3><ul><li>Have your main data file ready. Port, spatial, gridded, and auxiliary files are optional.</li><li>Choose a FishSET folder where project files can be saved.</li><li>For mapping or policy tabs, make sure your spatial data contain the required zone information.</li></ul></div>
<div class="quickstart-card"><h3>What gets saved</h3><ul><li>Project data and edits are stored in the local FishSET database.</li><li>Plots and tables are written to the project output folder.</li><li>Function calls and input values are written to the project logs.</li><li>The report template is stored in the project <code>doc</code> folder.</li></ul></div>
</div>

<div class="quickstart-note"><strong>Open the app:</strong> run <code>library(FishSET)</code> and then <code>run_fishset_gui()</code> in R or RStudio. The main data table is required; supporting files depend on your workflow.</div>

<h2>Quick path through the app</h2>

<div class="quickstart-path">
<p><em>Click any step below to expand the instructions.</em></p>
<details><summary><strong>Information across all tabs</strong></summary><p>All tabs include controls to close the app, refresh data, save plots and tables to the project <code>output</code> folder, record notes, and run an R expression. Within the app, the primary data frame is called <code>values$dataset</code>. Refreshing restores the original loaded table unless another table is selected on the <strong>Upload Data</strong> tab.</p></details>

<details><summary><strong>Upload Data</strong></summary><h4>Load Files</h4><ol><li>Click <strong>Change FishSET Folder</strong> to set where project files will be stored.</li><li>Type a new project name or select an existing project.</li><li>Provide the primary data; port and auxiliary data are optional.</li><li>Provide spatial data as a standard file or shapefile; gridded data are optional.</li><li>Click <strong>Load data</strong>.</li></ol><h4>Select Variables</h4><p>Use the Main and Spatial data sections to assign IDs, coordinates, and dates, then click <strong>Save selected variables</strong>. Use the <strong>Create ID</strong> buttons if trip, haul, or zone IDs are missing.</p><p><strong>Tip:</strong> Confidentiality settings, log reset, metadata, table management, and full data refresh are also available in this tab.</p></details>

<details><summary><strong>QAQC</strong></summary><h4>Data Quality Checks</h4><p>Use the sidebar to check for missing values, empty variables, duplicate data, incorrect classes, outliers, and invalid spatial coordinates. Use <strong>Preview data</strong> and <strong>Summary table</strong> before applying corrections, and save revised data to the FishSET database when finished.</p><h4>Explore the Data</h4><p>Switch between tables and temporal, spatial, and correlation plots to understand the loaded data. Generated plots and tables are saved to the project output folder.</p></details>

<details><summary><strong>Format Data</strong></summary><h4>Compute New Variables</h4><p>Use the sidebar tools to create variables with R expressions, spatial metrics, trip summaries, aggregations, and group-level statistics. Follow the prompts, review the generated column, and save the revised data.</p><h4>Define Alternative Fishing Choices</h4><p>Define how the distance matrix between observed and alternative locations will be calculated. Select starting and alternative locations, set the minimum number of observations for a zone, name the matrix, and click <strong>Create alternative location matrix</strong>.</p><h4>Create Expected Catch Matrix</h4><p>Estimate expected catch or revenue for alternative fishing zones. Name the matrix, select the catch and optional price variables, link the alternative matrix, configure temporal and grouping settings, and click <strong>Create Expectations</strong>.</p><h4>Format Model Data</h4><p>Reshape project data into the long format required for modeling. Select variables and the alternative and expectations matrices, optionally integrate external data, configure missing-data handling, and click <strong>Run Format Data</strong>.</p></details>

<details><summary><strong>Modeling</strong></summary><h4>Model Design</h4><p>Create the design matrices for a discrete choice model. Name the design, select formatted data and model type, specify utility and optional catch formulas, and click <strong>Create Design Object</strong>.</p><h4>Model Fit</h4><p>Select a saved model design, provide an optional fit name, choose an EPM distribution when required, and click <strong>Fit Model</strong>. Use the model comparison controls to review saved fits side by side.</p><h4>Model Cross Validation</h4><p>Select a model design and number of folds, then click <strong>Run Cross-Validation</strong> to assess out-of-sample predictive performance. Review overall metrics, fold accuracy, and estimated coefficients.</p></details>

<details><summary><strong>Policy</strong></summary><h4>Zone Closure</h4><p>Select an alternative matrix, click zones on the map, adjust allowable catch percentages, enter a scenario name, and click <strong>Add closure</strong>.</p><h4>Run Policy Simulations</h4><p>Select a fitted model and closure scenarios, set simulation draws, provide the marginal utility of income when required, and click <strong>Run Simulation</strong>.</p><h4>Summarize Effort Redistribution</h4><p>Extract and visualize how fishing effort shifts geographically under policy simulations.</p><h4>Summarize Welfare Impacts</h4><p>Evaluate expected welfare changes or compensating variation resulting from policy simulations.</p></details>

<details><summary><strong>Bookmark Choices</strong></summary><p><em>Under development.</em> Store choices and actions made in the FishSET GUI so they can be reloaded later.</p></details>
</div>
